paper_metadata.title: Design of low mass density γ/γ′ CoNi-based superalloys with promising high-temperature mechanical properties

evidence.quote: We report new compositions of CoNi-based superalloys that have low mass densities (7.84–8.20 g /cc), negative γ/ γ′ lattice misﬁt, and high γ′ solvus temperature up to 1094 °C
here, we report low mass density CoNi-based superalloys with primary constituents of Co, Ni, Al, Cr, and Nb

Alloys with nominal compositions of Co-30Ni-10Al-2Nb-5Cr and Co-30Ni-10Al-2Nb-xCr-yTi with varied content of Ti and Cr (x = 5, 8, 12 and y = 2, 4, all in at. %) were prepared by vacuum arc melting under inert argon atmosphere in 50 g batches using 4 N purity (99.99 at. %) constituent elements.

Subsequently, the arc-melted ingots were cast into rods (3 mm diameter × 80 mm length) for microstructural analyses and compression tests using a vacuum suction casting unit attached with a water-cooled split copper mold.
The cast rods were solutionized by isothermally holding at 1200 °C for 20 h in a vacuum furnace (vacuum of >10 –5 mbar) and were water quenched.

The aging of the solutionized rods was carried out under vacuum at 900 °C for different durations. For long-term microstructural stability and coarsening studies, the solutionized samples were vacuum sealed in quartz ampoules and heat treated at 900 °C for 50, 300, 500, and 1000 h followed by water quenching.
